title: Slow Through the Mist
logline: High in the hills the fog comes down so thick that a train driver and a signalman can see only a few metres ahead. The only way through is to slow down and look.

object.note: Object 4 (identity not chosen) may appear subtly, for example among Chathura's things while he travels, waits or watches, only where it sits naturally in a real moment. Never staged, never the subject.

thread_in.thread: If even the master is still learning, the way out of the fog is not certainty; in the high hills the fog is literal, and the only way through is to slow down and look.

thread_out.thread: The turn: having slowed down in the fog, the series looks at a single moment up close, in a shed where cinnamon quills are judged by smell, touch and sound before a word is spoken.

lesson.in_simple_terms: When you cannot see far, the way through is to slow down and look carefully at what is right in front of you. The texts describe confusion as something that darkens the mind, and name calm as the opposite of restlessness.
lesson.in_simple_terms_si: මීදුමේදී මෙන්ම සිත අඳුරු වූ විටත්, ඉදිරියට යා හැක්කේ වේගය අඩු කර ළඟ ඇති දේ හොඳින් බලමින්ය.
lesson.the_teaching: The Abhidhamma describes delusion (moha) as a quality that darkens the mind so that it cannot know a thing as it really is, and the hindrances (nīvaraṇa) as covers that keep the mind from wholesome states. Pradeepika names calm (samatha) as the opposite of restlessness and remorse, and says that when the mind keeps hold of one object without agitation, concentration can arise. It also says that as darkness goes when light rises, ignorance goes when understanding appears.
lesson.how_the_film_shows_it: Fog rolls across the platform and swallows the rails, and passengers stare into nothing but white. The signalman's tokens, bells and lamps, and the driver's few metres of track at a low, steady speed, show a real practice of moving through what cannot be seen one careful step at a time. If the cloud thins and the valley appears, the film lets that light arrive on its own.

key_terms.en: delusion; the darkening of mind that prevents knowing a thing as it is
one-pointedness; the power to stay with one object

lesson.caution: The fog is only an image of that darkening; slowing down is the workers' real safety practice, not a technique the texts promise will clear delusion, which they say only path-knowledge uproots.
lesson.builds_on: If even the master is still learning, the way out is not certainty; this film turns the whole group's fog literal and shows the first step out: slowing down to look.
lesson.evidence_class: editorial interpretation grounded in cited source teaching
